canonical_title: The Selected Letters of Philip K. Dick: 1977-1979
author: Philip K. Dick (edited by Don Herron, introduction by Robert Anton Wilson)
card_summary: The Underwood-Miller volume for 1977-1979, edited by Don Herron with an introduction by Robert Anton Wilson, covering the Metz festival, the deepening Exegesis, and PKD's letters on Jaynes, Star Wars, and revealed religion.
page_summary:
This volume of the Selected Letters gathers Philip K. Dick's correspondence from 1977 through 1979, edited by Don Herron and introduced by Robert Anton Wilson. The period includes PKD's celebrated appearance at the Metz science-fiction festival in France, where he delivered his talk on orthogonal time and alternate worlds, and the ongoing labor of the Exegesis at home in Santa Ana.

The letters of these years show PKD reaching outward for frameworks to explain 2-3-74: his March 1977 letter to Julian Jaynes on the bicameral mind, his 1977 letters to Eugene Warren reading Star Wars as Christian myth made literal, and his exchanges with scholars such as Patricia Warrick. Beneath the theology runs the steady business of a novelist at work on the books that would become the VALIS material.

The volume documents the middle stretch of PKD's late religious project, when he was actively borrowing and testing outside theories against his own experience.
